column1: # The corpus cases that are recorded on the wire, and why each one is here.
# The cut is not "as many as fit". A wire capture answers one question
# an in-memory serialisation call cannot: what the product's own
# transport layer does to the octets on the way out. The first
# twenty-three rows below are the construct families where the inventory
# carried a divergence or a setting, plus every family where the two
# levels *could* part — anything with an alignment gap, anything with an
# encapsulation field, anything whose byte order is a decision.
# The rest are here for a second reason, and it is not the same one.
# twenty-three cases produced is cited by **seven** of them in the row's
# own text — A4, A5, B4, B5, C3, H8, N12 — and by three more, D3, D4 and
# D5, in the run's own section and not in their rows. Either way it is
# the same shape: a hundred and thirty-odd behaviours whose only
# A behaviour that only ever appears in an in-memory assertion is a
# claim about a serialiser, not about a product: it cannot see the
# encapsulation identifier an RTPS layer is free to replace, the
# trailing padding that layer adds, the inline QoS a writer sends, or a
# front end that serialises a type its `create_datawriter` then refuses.
# So every behaviour that a **writer** can put on a socket gets a case,
# whether or not the inventory expected a divergence there — and
# `coverage.tsv` names, for each of the 146, either the cases below that
# reach it or the one-line reason no capture can.
#   case       the corpus directory under tests/interop-corpus/
#   domain     the DDS domain id this case runs on. One domain per case
#              means one UDP port range per case, which is how a packet
#              is attributed to a case — by the port it arrived on and
#              not by when it arrived. The CORBA runners use 12300+id.
#              The ids cycle through twenty slots, 20 to 39, because
#              DDSI-RTPS §9.6.1.1 puts domain 233's ports past 65535 and
#              `--domain-offset` has to fit nine implementations running
#              at once above whatever the highest case uses. Two cases
#              twenty rows apart share a slot and never share a run:
#              within one implementation the loop is sequential.
#   control    `longer` when the poison sample is longer than the real
#              one, so the real sample's fill spans land on octets the
#              poison wrote and a `00` there is an octet the peer wrote.
#              `equal` when the two samples have the same layout:
#              nothing can then write the other's fill, and the case
#              says nothing about fill provenance — its fill column
#              poison files carry `longer` where the type allows it —
#              ten of the twenty-three, the other thirteen being types
#              with no variable-length member; the generated ones
#              (`make-poison.py`) mutate numeric leaves, or rotate an
#              enumerator inside its own declaration where the sample
#              has no numeric leaf at all, and are all `equal`, which is
#              a limit of the generator and not of the capture.
#   rows       the wire-feature-inventory rows the case bears on
